mainTopic: Marrying a דומה or her daughter; the court's warning to a סוטה; comparing husband and wife in the סוטה laws
overview: The amud opens by finishing an argument about whom it is better to marry. One view says to marry a דומה (a woman suspected of promiscuity) rather than her daughter, who might be a ממזרת. רבי יוחנן says the opposite: marry the daughter, who keeps her חזקת כשרות. רבא reads a challenging ברייתא as allowing a דומה only after the fact. The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, because רב תחליפא taught that most relations of a married woman are presumed to be with her husband. רב עמרם asks whether this holds for an extremely promiscuous wife, and the question ends in תיקו. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about the court warning a wife whose husband cannot. The רבנן and רבי יוסי argue whether that warning can lead to drinking the bitter water. Finally, a ברייתא compares husband and wife in the סוטה laws: רב ששת rules that a blind wife does not drink, and רב אשי begins a second example that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Marry the suspected woman, not her daughter
steps.stepSummary: The end of the first opinion: a man should marry a דומה but not a בת דומה, because the daughter may come from forbidden seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A man should marry] a woman people talk about as promiscuous, and not marry the daughter of such a woman. The woman herself was born from a kosher father, but the daughter may have been born from a forbidden relationship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that started on the previous page. It says it is better to marry a suspected woman than to marry her daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern here is the family line, not behavior. The suspected woman herself was born to a proper family. Her daughter, though, might be the child of an affair, which would make her a ממזרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman about whom people talk, suspecting her of promiscuity
The daughter of such a woman
Literally 'a kosher drop'; a child of a proper relationship
Literally 'a flawed drop'; possibly a child of a forbidden relationship

steps.confusionAlert: The beginning words ('A man should marry...') are on the previous page. This page opens in the middle of that sentence.

phrases.english: [A man should marry] a woman suspected of promiscuity,
phrases.notes: This sentence started on the previous page with ריש לקיש saying 'ישא אדם', meaning 'a man should marry'.

phrases.english: and not marry the daughter of a suspected woman.
For this one comes from kosher seed,
and that one comes from flawed seed.
phrases.notes: He means the daughter might be from an affair, which would make her a ממזרת.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prefer marrying a דומה over a בת דומה, because the daughter's lineage is in doubt.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says to marry the daughter, who keeps her clean status, and not the suspected woman herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A man should marry the daughter of a suspected woman, and not the suspected woman herself. The daughter keeps her presumption of being proper, but the suspected woman has lost hers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees and reverses the advice. He says to marry the daughter, not the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן looks at the woman's own status, her חזקה. The daughter did nothing wrong and keeps a clean חזקה. The suspected woman's own reputation has damaged her חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption that a person is proper and fit
Literally 'stands'; remains in that status

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:
A man should marry the daughter of a suspected woman,
and not marry a suspected woman.
For this one stands in a presumption of being proper,
and that one does not stand in a presumption of being proper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 1 and reverses its advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prefer marrying a בת דומה over a דומה, because the daughter keeps her חזקת כשרות.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to allow marrying a suspected woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a man may marry a דומה, which seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'A man may marry a suspected woman!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא. The ברייתא seems to say that marrying a suspected woman is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said not to marry a דומה. The ברייתא says a man may marry a דומה. Read simply, the two contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Marries

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A man may marry a suspected woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that one should not marry a דומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly permits marrying a דומה, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא means after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא cannot mean that marrying a דומה is fine to begin with. It must mean that if he already married her, the marriage stands. He also has the ברייתא mention a בת דומה, the case that is fine לכתחילה, as רבי יוחנן says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do you really think it means he may marry her to begin with?! Rather, it means 'if he married her' it is fine. Also teach 'the daughter of a suspected woman' in the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רבי יוחנן. He explains that the ברייתא is talking about a marriage that already happened, not giving advice beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody would advise marrying a suspected woman to begin with, so the ברייתא must mean בדיעבד: if it already happened, the marriage is acceptable. Read this way, it does not argue with רבי יוחנן's לכתחילה advice. Since the ברייתא is being fixed anyway, רבא also has it mention a בת דומה, whom one may marry even לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And do you really think so?!', a rhetorical rejection of the simple reading
To begin with, before acting
If he already married, after the fact (בדיעבד)

phrases.english: רבא said:
And do you really think he may marry her to begin with?!
Rather: if he married her [it is acceptable],
and also teach: 'the daughter of a suspected woman.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא as talking about after the fact (בדיעבד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא permits marrying a דומה to begin with.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only says that a marriage already made is acceptable, so רבי יוחנן stands.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that a man should marry a בת דומה and not a דומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: A man should marry the daughter of a suspected woman, and not marry a suspected woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling, and it follows רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two opinions, the practical ruling sides with רבי יוחנן. The next step gives the source that supports this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the הלכה is', the final practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה: better to marry the daughter of a suspected woman than the suspected woman herself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical guide for choosing a marriage partner when there are rumors about a family.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is:
A man should marry the daughter of a suspected woman,
and not marry a suspected woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument from Steps 1 and 2 in favor of רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן: marry a בת דומה, not a דומה.

steps.title: Proof: most relations are with the husband
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא taught that the children of an unfaithful wife are כשרים, because most relations are presumed to be with the husband. So the daughter's lineage is not a worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב תחליפא from the West taught before רבי אבהו: If a woman is unfaithful, her children are כשרים, because most relations are attributed to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that supports the ruling. It removes the fear about the daughter's lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion's worry was that the daughter might be a ממזרת. This teaching says we follow the majority (רוב): most of a wife's relations are with her husband. So her children are presumed to be his and fully כשרים, and that worry falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: From the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
A married woman who is unfaithful
Most relations are attributed to the husband
Of proper, unflawed lineage

steps.whatToRemember: Because of רוב, children of a married woman are presumed to be her husband's, even if she is suspected of unfaithfulness.

phrases.english: As רב תחליפא from the West taught
before רבי אבהו:
A woman who is unfaithful:
her children are of proper lineage,
because most relations are attributed to the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר מַעְרְבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and source for the ruling in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a בת דומה may be married
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב תחליפא's teaching that the children of an unfaithful wife are כשרים, because of רוב

steps.title: רב עמרם asks about an extremely promiscuous wife
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם asks whether רב תחליפא's rule still holds when the wife is extremely promiscuous. He first rules out one opinion, where there is nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם asked: what if she was extremely promiscuous? According to the view that a woman conceives only near her period, there is no question, because the husband doesn't know when that is and doesn't watch her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם tests the limit of the rule from step 6 by asking about an extreme case. He then removes one opinion from the question, which sets up where the real question lies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said most relations are presumed to be with the husband. If the wife is extremely promiscuous, that "most" may no longer be true. If conception happens near her period, the husband cannot know that time ahead of time and cannot guard her then, so for that view there is nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: asked a question he was unsure about
extremely promiscuous
a woman's regular time of menstruation
guards, watches over

phrases.english: Rav Amram asked:
If she was extremely promiscuous, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means: are her children still assumed to be the husband's, like in רב תחליפא's rule?

phrases.english: According to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אִשָּׁה מִתְעַבֶּרֶת אֶלָּא סָמוּךְ לְוִוסְתָּהּ
phrases.english: a woman becomes pregnant only close to her period
you need not ask,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא יָדַע בַּהּ וְלָא מְנַטַּר לַהּ.
phrases.english: since he does not know that time and does not guard her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limit of רב תחליפא's presumption from step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the presumption that children belong to the husband still apply when the wife is extremely promiscuous?

steps.title: The real question: the view that conception is near immersion
steps.stepSummary: The question only applies to the view that a woman conceives near her immersion. Since the husband knows that time, maybe he guards her then. Or maybe he can't guard someone so promiscuous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is the question? According to the view that a woman conceives only near her immersion. Since he knows that time, does he guard her carefully? Or perhaps, since she is extremely promiscuous, he can't?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the real question and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If conception happens near her טבילה, the husband knows exactly when that is. So he may watch her closely then, and the children would be his. The other side is that someone extremely promiscuous cannot be guarded well enough, even at a known time.

keyTerms.meaning: immersion in a מקוה after her period
he watches very carefully
or perhaps (the other side of a question)

phrases.english: When should you ask?
According to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אִשָּׁה מִתְעַבֶּרֶת אֶלָּא סָמוּךְ לִטְבִילָתָהּ, מַאי?
phrases.english: a woman becomes pregnant only close to her immersion, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּיָדַע בָּהּ, נַטּוֹרֵי מְנַטַּר לָהּ,
phrases.english: Since he knows that time, he watches her carefully;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֵּיוָן דִּפְרוּצָה בְּיוֹתֵר — לָא?
phrases.english: or perhaps, since she is extremely promiscuous, he cannot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 7 to the one opinion where it applies
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If the husband knows the time of conception, does his guarding keep the presumption alive even for a very promiscuous wife?

steps.title: The question is left unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: רב עמרם's question remains unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רב עמרם's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source is found that decides either side. So it stays a doubt whether the children of an extremely promiscuous wife are assumed to be the husband's, under the immersion view.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רב תחליפא's rule (children are the husband's) is clear for an ordinary unfaithful wife. For an extremely promiscuous wife the question was left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in steps 7 and 8

steps.title: The court warns wives of husbands who cannot warn them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about women whom the court warns. A ברייתא learns from "איש איש" that this includes wives of a deaf-mute, a שוטה, an insane man, a man overseas, or a prisoner. The warning makes them lose their כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "And these are the women whom the court warns." The רבנן taught: why does the verse say "איש איש" (any man) instead of just "איש"? To include the wife of a deaf-mute, of a שוטה, of an insane man, one whose husband went overseas, and one whose husband is in prison. The court warns them so that they lose their כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that gives the verse source for the court warning a wife in place of her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the husband gives the קינוי (warning). The extra word "איש" in the verse teaches that when a husband cannot warn her, the court may do it for him. Here the result of that warning is that if she then secludes herself with the man, she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse teaches
to include
a deaf-mute
an insane or confused person
issue a קינוי, a formal warning
the marriage-contract payment owed to the wife

phrases.english: "And these are the women whom the court" etc.
The Rabbis taught:
It could have said "a man"; why does the verse say "any man"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:12. The word איש is doubled there, and the ברייתא learns from the extra word.

phrases.english: To include the wife of a deaf-mute, and the wife of an imbecile,
and the wife of an insane person,
and one whose husband went overseas,
and one whose husband was locked in prison:
the court warns them
to disqualify them from their marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learned from "איש איש": the court may warn a wife whose husband cannot, and that warning makes her lose her כתובה.

steps.title: The court's warning does not make her drink
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the idea that the court's warning also leads to the bitter water. The verse says "the man shall bring his wife," so only the husband's warning does that.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the court's warning also lets her be made to drink. So the verse says: "And the man shall bring his wife."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible extension of the rule and then rules it out from a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the court's warning works fully, like the husband's. The verse ties the drinking to "the man" bringing "his wife," so the court's warning only affects her כתובה. It cannot lead to the drinking of the bitter water.

keyTerms.meaning: one might have thought
to make them drink the bitter water

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two results. The court's warning makes her lose her כתובה, but according to this ברייתא it does NOT lead to her drinking the bitter water.

phrases.english: One might think the warning works even to make them drink;
therefore the verse says:
"Then the man shall bring his wife."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far the court's warning from step 10 reaches
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the court's warning leads to drinking
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse links the drinking only to the husband bringing his own wife

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the court's warning can lead to drinking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees. The court's warning also leads to drinking, and when the husband gets out of prison, he brings her to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: the warning works even to make her drink, and when her husband gets out of prison, he makes her drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives an opposing opinion to the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the court's warning works fully, like a husband's. The verse "the man shall bring" is still kept, because the drinking waits until the husband himself is free to bring her.

keyTerms.meaning: he will make her drink
prison

steps.whatToRemember: The court may warn a wife whose husband cannot. Everyone agrees this costs her the כתובה. The תנא קמא says it cannot lead to drinking. רבי יוסי says it can, once the husband is released and brings her himself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: the warning works even to make her drink,
and when her husband comes out of prison, he makes her drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against the limit set in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court's warning can lead to drinking; the husband brings her once he is free.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lies underneath the argument between the רבנן and רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument it just quoted. This is a setup line; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 showed the רבנן saying only the husband's warning leads to drinking. Step 12 showed רבי יוסי saying the court's warning also counts. Now the גמרא wants to find the exact idea they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: On what do they disagree?

phrases.english: On what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root of the argument quoted in steps 11-12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the argument of the רבנן and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Must the one who warns also be the one who brings her?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן require the same person to warn and to bring her. רבי יוסי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that we need "he warned... and he shall bring" to be the same person. רבי יוסי holds that we do not need this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: they argue about how to read the פסוק "וקנא... והביא".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן read the פסוק as one connected act: the man who warns is the man who brings. So if the court warned, the husband cannot bring her to drink. רבי יוסי says the two parts can be done by different people, so the court can warn and the husband can later bring her.

keyTerms.meaning: And he warned (the husband's jealousy warning)
And he shall bring (her to the כהן)
We require

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: warner and bringer must be the same person. רבי יוסי: they can be different people.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: we require "and he warned... and he shall bring,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14–15. The same man who warns her must be the one who brings her.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
we do not require "and he warned... and he shall bring."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether the warning and the bringing must be done by the same person.

steps.title: The verse compares husband and wife
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "אשר תשטה אשה תחת אישה" that the man and woman are compared to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "when a wife goes astray while under her husband" comes to compare a man to a woman and a woman to a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It says a פסוק links husband and wife together in the סוטה laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש means rules that apply to one side also apply to the other side. The ברייתא does not yet say which rules; that is what the גמרא will ask next.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare (to learn one case from another through a פסוק)
Goes astray

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"when a wife goes astray while under her husband,"
to compare a man to a woman
and a woman to a man.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׂטֶה אִשָּׁה תַּחַת אִישָׁהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the argument of the רבנן and רבי יוסי is explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק compares husband and wife to each other in the סוטה laws.

steps.title: What law does the comparison teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law comes out of comparing husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law is this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this comparison actually teaches us. This sets up the answers of רב ששת and רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison is only useful if it changes some law. The גמרא wants a concrete case.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law?

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical use of the היקש in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law is learned from comparing husband and wife.

steps.title: A blind wife does not drink
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת: a blind husband cannot make her drink, so a blind wife does not drink either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Just as if he is blind he would not have her drink, as it says "and it was hidden from the eyes of her husband," so too she, if she was blind, would not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the first answer: blindness disqualifies the wife just as it disqualifies the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "ונעלם מעיני אישה" shows the husband must have eyes, so a blind husband is left out. The היקש carries this over to the wife: a blind wife also does not drink.

keyTerms.meaning: Blind person
And it was hidden from the eyes of her husband
Has her drink

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Just as if he is blind
he would not have her drink,
as it is written: "and it was hidden from the eyes of her husband,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13. The husband has to be someone with eyes that could have seen.

phrases.english: so too she, if she was blind,
she would not drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִם הוּא סוֹמֵא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blindness disqualifies the wife from drinking, learned from the husband.

steps.title: רב אשי starts with a lame woman or a woman without hands
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי begins another answer: a lame woman or a woman without hands does not drink, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Just as a lame woman and a woman without hands would not drink, as it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second example of the comparison. This time he starts from the woman's side; his פסוק and conclusion come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת went from husband to wife. רב אשי starts with a rule about the wife, so it seems he will carry it over to the husband, showing the comparison works both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: A lame woman
A woman without hands

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Just as a lame woman and a woman without hands
would not drink,
as it is written:
phrases.notes: The פסוק itself comes at the top of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁחִיגֶּרֶת וְגִידֶּמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 16, alongside רב ששת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begins showing that a lame woman or one without hands does not drink, as the basis for the comparison.
